newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan life insurers disclose 1996/97 bad loans.
newsitem.headline: Japan life insurers disclose 1996/97 bad loans.

text.p: Japan's top eight life insurance companies unveiled on Monday the size of their outstanding problem loans as of March 31, 1997.
Outstanding problem loans as of March 31, 1997 were as follows (in billions of yen unless specified, with year-ago comparisons):

The figures comprise loans to bankrupt firms, loans with interest payments in arrears by six months or more, loans on which interest rates have been cut to help cooperate restructuring, as well as those to troubled clients.

The full names of the life insurers are Meiji Life Insurance Co, Asahi Mutual Life Insurance Co, Sumitomo Life Insurance Co, Dai-Ichi Mutual Life Insurance Co, Nippon Life Insurance Co, Mitsui Mutual Life Insurance Co, Yasuda Mutual Life Insurance Co, and Chiyoda Mutual Life Insurance Co. All the life insurers are unlisted.
